resources.string: If you force-stop this app, or set its battery use to “Restricted”, a copied password stays on the clipboard until you open the app again.
Never pin a password in your keyboard’s clipboard: pinned items are never removed.
Your PIN and fingerprint
Anyone whose fingerprint is saved in this phone’s settings can open the app.
Don’t use your phone’s unlock PIN or your bank card PIN as the app PIN. Someone who knows it could open the app.
On a rooted phone, someone can try every PIN in a few hours. Your master password still protects your passwords, so make it strong and never use it anywhere else.

Someone who knows your PIN can choose a new master password for the app. It starts working only after 24 hours with the phone switched on, and until then the app tells you about it each time you open it. If it wasn’t you, tap “Cancel it” and change your PIN.
What the app cannot protect you from
A phone that has been hacked or “rooted”, a harmful keyboard app, or an app you allowed to control your phone (accessibility).
Passwords shown as dots stay hidden from other apps, even from an app that may control your phone. On Android 13 and older, such an app can read a password while you show it on the screen.

Never install an app file (APK) sent to you in Telegram or offered by a website, even if it seems to come from someone you know. Never let an app control your phone (accessibility) unless you need it because of a disability.
Never use “Clear storage” to fix a problem with your PIN: it deletes your passwords, and the ones from before a replaced master password with them.
Anyone who has your unlocked phone can delete the app, and your passwords with it. Only a backup kept outside the phone survives that.
If your phone is lost or stolen, your passwords stay locked. After 5 wrong PINs in a row the PIN is turned off, and then only your fingerprint or your master password opens the app.

To get your passwords on a new phone, install %1$s there, tap “Restore from a backup file”, choose your newest backup and type your master password. Without a backup, your passwords can’t be brought back.
Moving your apps to a new phone, for example with “Copy apps and data”, does not bring your passwords. Make a backup on the old phone and restore it on the new one.
If %1$s on the new phone says “Welcome back”, type your master password once. Then choose a PIN for the new phone.
Make a new backup whenever you have added or changed passwords. Keep it outside this phone: in Google Drive, on a computer, or sent to yourself.
Nobody can reset your master password: it is not stored anywhere.
If your PIN or fingerprint still opens the app, open it and choose a new master password: Settings › App lock › Change master password › I don’t remember it.

The new master password starts working after 24 hours with the phone switched on. The countdown stops while the phone is switched off, so open the app in the morning and again in the evening. Until then, open the app with your PIN or fingerprint as usual.
Then make a new backup. Your old backups still open only with your old master password.
If someone else replaced your master password, your own still opens your passwords as they were: “Forgot master password?”, then “Open my passwords from before …”.

If you can’t open the app at all: try the words on your paper, or restore a backup whose master password you remember. You can also start with an empty app. Your old passwords stay on the phone, locked, in case you remember the password later.
Tap “Forgot PIN? Use master password”, type your master password, and choose a new PIN.
After 5 wrong PINs in a row, the PIN is turned off. Nothing is deleted: type your master password, then choose a new PIN.

resources.string: Samsung phones keep a list of copied text. To keep passwords out of it, turn off or clear the clipboard history in Samsung Keyboard settings.
Some keyboards keep their own list of copied text; you can turn it off in the keyboard’s settings.
